column1: # base:dung_pat (Plants' ecology loop: grazers leave it, it rots to a grass tuft). A low box [2,0,2]-[14,1.5,14]: the top shows texels 4-28 of the tile, the side only its bottom 3 rows. BLOCK_LIKE: grass_top,dirt,<item dung>

column3: dung_pat_top|face|A cow pat seen from above, filling the middle 24 by 24 px of the square (the rest the same brown, it is cut away): a round flat pat, dark olive-brown (#2e2618 #3e3420 #50442a #625436), with concentric slumped rings, a network of dry cracks, the rim drier and paler (#7a6a48 #8e7e58) and slightly lifted, a few pale straw grass bits (#b0a060) mixed in, light from the top left
column4: dung_pat_side|cube|The side of a thin cow pat: a band of the same dark olive-brown dung (#2e2618 #3e3420 #50442a #625436), fibrous and lumpy, a drier paler crust along the top edge (#7a6a48), a few straw bits, seamless left to right

column1: # dung_pat_top: after the cut, the corners outside an irregular round edge (radius about 11.5 texels) made clear in code, so the box's square top reads as a round pat over the grass (register the block as cutout).
